newsitem.title: MOLDOVA: Moldovan Communists back Lucinschi in run-off.
newsitem.headline: Moldovan Communists back Lucinschi in run-off.

text.p: Moldova's Communists threw their weight behind parliamentary chairman Petru Lucinschi on Thursday in a bid to defeat incumbent Mircea Snegur in the run-off for the presidency.

"We do not view Lucinschi as an ideal politician, but each vote cast for him is a vote against Snegur, who is leading Moldova to totalitarian rule and the loss of independence," Communist Party leader Vladimir Voronin told a news conference.
Snegur took first place in Sunday's first-round ballot with 39 percent of the votes, Lucinschi was second with 28 and Voronin came in third with 10.

The Communist leader is the second major candidate to back Lucinschi for the run-off on December 1. Prime Minister Andrei Sangheli, who received just nine percent of the votes, joined Lucinschi's team on Tuesday
Voronin said he had taken his decision after talks with Lucinschi on Wednesday.
"The Communists insisted only that Lucinschi safeguards Moldova's independence and integrity and the Moldovans as a nation. Now we have no time for other claims," Voronin said.
Sangheli said his government would resign after the second round.

"I am ready to tender my resignation after the election of a new president...to preserve peace and order in the republic," the prime minister said in a Wednesday night television address. "This is both my personal decision and that of the whole government."
Political analysts said support from Sangheli and Voronin would boost Lucinschi's chances in the second round.
Snegur, who called for a "nationwide front against communist and revanchist forces", has one remaining possible ally, nationalist Valeriu Matei.
Matei said on Tuesday he needed to consult his Party of Democratic Forces before deciding whether to back Snegur.

Snegur and Lucinschi, both 56 and senior Communist Party leaders in Soviet days, present two different visions of the future for Moldova, a landlocked state of 4.3 million people between Romania and Ukraine.
Centre-right Snegur wants closer ties with the West and with Moldova's ethnic kin in Romania. He is seeking changes in the constitution to boost presidential powers.
Left-leaning Lucinschi does not intend to amend the law. He seeks equally close ties with Romania and Russia, on which Moldova heavily depends for supplies of fuel and energy.

"Today Snegur is backed by the pro-Romanian Popular Front, which has become even more embittered, intolerant and impatient in its main goal -- merger with Romania. Let's support Lucinschi to defend our sovreignty and independence," Voronin said.
